templates.name: authelia
templates.title: Authelia
templates.description: Sign-in with a second factor, in front of apps with no login of their own. Needs HTTPS and a domain. Sign in with the admin from the inputs, then register a second factor: the one-time code it asks for comes by mail when a mail server is set, else it shows in the stack's logs (the notifications service). To protect an app, add Caddy's forward_auth to it, as Authelia's Caddy guide shows.

inputs.name: DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain of its sign-in page, e.g. auth.example.org

inputs.name: COOKIE_DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain to protect, e.g. example.org
inputs.description: Must contain the domain above. Apps under it share the sign-in.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: The admin signs in with it. Authelia gets only its hash. Changing it here changes it on the next apply.

inputs.name: SMTP_ADDRESS
inputs.title: Mail server, e.g. submission://smtp.example.org:587
inputs.description: Optional. submission:// for STARTTLS (port 587), submissions:// for TLS (port 465). Without one, the one-time codes show in the stack's logs.

inputs.name: SMTP_SENDER
inputs.title: Mail from, e.g. Authelia <auth@example.org>
inputs.description: By default noreply at the protected domain.

templates.name: backrest
templates.title: Backrest (restic)
templates.description: Deduplicated, encrypted restic backups with a web UI and schedules, e.g. offsite to a Storage Box over SFTP or any rclone remote. Docker volumes are mounted read-only under /userdata/volumes. It starts with the admin from the stack's inputs, so no first-run setup is offered. Add a repository and a backup plan in the UI.

inputs.name: EXTRA_PATH
inputs.title: Additional host folder to back up (read-only)

inputs.name: BACKREST_USERNAME
inputs.title: Admin user name
inputs.description: Used only on the first start, when Backrest has no config yet. Later, change users in Backrest's settings.

inputs.name: BACKREST_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: You sign in to the web UI with it. Used only on the first start; stacks already set up in the UI keep the admin they have.

inputs.name: BACKREST_INSTANCE
inputs.title: Instance name
inputs.description: Names this Backrest in its snapshots; give each host that writes to the same repository its own. Used only on the first start, and can't be changed later.

templates.name: beszel
templates.title: Beszel
templates.description: Lightweight host and container metrics, with history and alerts. This is the hub; sign in with the admin set here. Each host to watch runs an agent: the beszel-agent template.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin e-mail (you sign in with it)

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet. Beszel creates this admin on its first start; change the password later in Beszel.

templates.name: beszel-agent
templates.title: Beszel agent
templates.description: Sends this host's and its containers' metrics to a Beszel hub. In the hub, Add System with the WebSocket option gives the key and token. It connects out to the hub and opens no port, and reads Docker through a read-only proxy. Network traffic is the container's own, not the host's.

inputs.name: KEY
inputs.title: The hub's public key (from Add System)

templates.name: binfmt
templates.title: Foreign-architecture emulation
templates.description: Registers QEMU user-mode emulators, so images built for another CPU (e.g. amd64 on an arm64 host) can run, slower. Registrations do not survive a reboot, so nepfleet serve starts this stack again when it starts and the emulators are missing (NepFleet 0.2 or later). Privileged.

templates.name: caddy
templates.title: Caddy ingress
templates.description: Reverse proxy with automatic TLS. Routes are read from caddy.* labels, and DNS-01 gives trusted certificates on home networks too.

inputs.name: CADDY_DNS_PROVIDER
inputs.title: DNS provider for DNS-01
inputs.description: Needed for trusted certificates on names that are not reachable from the internet (home network) and for wildcards.

inputs.name: DNS_API_TOKEN
inputs.title: DNS provider API token
inputs.description: Not needed without a DNS provider. Details per provider: nepfleet docs/home-tls.md.

help.cloudflare: Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token. Permissions: Zone → Zone → Read and Zone → DNS → Edit. Zone Resources: Include → Specific zone → your zone. That also covers the sites' records when "Create the sites' DNS records" is on.
help.desec: deSEC → Token management → a new token without "Can manage tokens". For certificates alone, a policy that allows only TXT records is enough; with "Create the sites' DNS records" on, also allow A and AAAA.
help.hetzner: Hetzner Console → your project → Security → API tokens → Generate, with Read & Write. Put the DNS zone in a project of its own: the token reaches everything in its project.

inputs.name: DNS_RECORDS
inputs.title: Create the sites' DNS records
inputs.description: With on, Caddy keeps an A record (and AAAA, with IPv6) for each of its sites under the DNS zone pointed at this host's public address, through the DNS provider and its token (which then needs DNS edit on the zone, as for certificates). It checks every 5 minutes, finds the address by asking public what-is-my-IP services, and sets records that point elsewhere to this host. It never touches the zone's apex, and never deletes records. Works with every DNS provider here. Single hosts only: in Swarm, leave it off (replicas would overwrite each other's records).

inputs.name: DNS_ZONE
inputs.title: DNS zone for the records
inputs.description: The domain the DNS provider holds, e.g. example.org: sites under it (status.vps.example.org) get records. Used when DNS records are on.

inputs.name: WILDCARD
inputs.title: One wildcard certificate for a home domain
inputs.description: Every certificate is published in Certificate Transparency logs, so one per name lists what runs at home publicly. With on, names under the wildcard domain share one certificate. Needs a DNS provider.

inputs.name: WILDCARD_DOMAIN
inputs.title: Wildcard domain
inputs.description: For example home.example.org: covers jellyfin.home.example.org, but not deeper names. Used when the wildcard is on.

templates.name: dozzle
templates.title: Dozzle
templates.description: Live container logs in the browser, behind a sign-in (the admin user and password set here). Deploy on swarm for a fleet-wide view.

inputs.name: DOZZLE_USERNAME
inputs.title: Admin user
inputs.description: Sign in to Dozzle with it.

inputs.name: DOZZLE_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet; Dozzle gets only its bcrypt hash. To change it, set a new one in the stack's secrets and apply.

inputs.name: ALERTS_API_URL
inputs.title: NepFleet's API for log alerts (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: NepFleet connects Dozzle to its own API. Log lines with fatal, panic or out of memory go there and on to the fleet's notification channels, deduplicated. Set it only to send alerts to another NepFleet, e.g. https://fleet.example.org.

inputs.name: ALERTS_TOKEN
inputs.title: API token for alerts (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: NepFleet makes a notify token for this stack (listed on Access as stack:dozzle/…). Set it only with an override URL: nepfleet token create --name dozzle --scope notify --expires 365d

templates.name: fail2ban
templates.title: fail2ban
templates.description: Bans addresses after repeated failed SSH logins, in the host's firewall. Privileged: it uses the host's network and changes its firewall, and reads the host's journal. It reacts after failures, so key-only SSH matters more (check with nepfleet doctor --security). Unban an address: docker exec <container> fail2ban-client set sshd unbanip <address>.

inputs.name: IGNORE_IP
inputs.title: Addresses never banned, separated by spaces
inputs.description: Private networks by default, so you can't lock yourself out from your LAN or VPN. Add the public address you connect from, if it is fixed.

templates.name: frpc
templates.title: frp client (home side)
templates.description: Publishes a local service through an frps on a public host. Add more [[proxies]] to frpc.toml in the fleet repository.

inputs.name: SERVER_ADDR
inputs.title: frps address
inputs.description: The public host's WireGuard IP.

inputs.name: FRP_TOKEN
inputs.title: frps token
inputs.description: The token you gave the frps stack (its FRP_TOKEN).

inputs.name: LOCAL_HOST
inputs.title: Local service host
inputs.description: Container name on the ingress network (e.g. jellyfin) or an IP.

templates.name: frps
templates.title: frp server (public side)
templates.description: Receives tunnels from frpc at home and publishes them through Caddy. Bind it to the WireGuard address, so the control port is never on the internet.

inputs.name: BIND_ADDR
inputs.title: Address for the frp control port
inputs.description: This host's WireGuard IP (recommended) or 0.0.0.0.

inputs.name: EXPOSED_HOSTS
inputs.title: Public host names served through tunnels
inputs.description: Comma separated, e.g. "jellyfin.example.org, photos.example.org"

inputs.name: FRP_TOKEN
inputs.title: Token for frpc
inputs.description: frpc stacks at home sign in with it: give them the same token. Kept encrypted in the fleet. A long random string, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 24

templates.name: grafana
templates.title: Grafana
templates.description: Metrics dashboards, reading the prometheus template's data. Sign in as admin, with the password in the stack's encrypted secrets (ADMIN_PASSWORD).

inputs.name: PROMETHEUS_URL
inputs.title: Prometheus address
inputs.description: The prometheus template's address on the ingress network.

inputs.name: LOKI_URL
inputs.title: Loki address
inputs.description: The loki template's address on the ingress network, for logs.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: You sign in as admin with it. Kept encrypted in the fleet. Grafana takes it on its first start; change it later in Grafana.

templates.name: homepage
templates.title: Homepage
templates.description: A dashboard for your services. Entries come from homepage.* labels; title, theme, language, search and the resource widgets are set as values (NepFleet owns settings.yaml, widgets.yaml, and services.yaml and bookmarks.yaml, which it keeps empty so Homepage shows none of its samples).

templates.name: loki
templates.title: Loki
templates.description: Keeps every container's logs on this host, searchable in Grafana by stack and service. Alloy collects them through a read-only Docker proxy. The grafana template has it as a data source already (http://loki:3100). Some apps log tokens or personal data, so treat the logs like the apps' own data. No usage reports go to Grafana Labs.

templates.name: neptide
templates.title: neptide image updates
templates.description: Health-gated image updates with automatic rollback, for containers and swarm services labelled neptide.enable=true.

inputs.name: DOCKER_GID
inputs.title: Docker group ID (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: NepFleet fills in the host's docker group. Set it only if neptide can't reach Docker (getent group docker | cut -d: -f3 on the host).

inputs.name: NOTIFY
inputs.title: Notification URLs (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: notifications go to NepFleet, which sends them to the fleet's notification channels. Set comma separated shoutrrr URLs (e.g. discord://token@webhookid) only to send somewhere else instead.

templates.name: pocket-id
templates.title: Pocket ID
templates.description: Sign in with passkeys across your apps: a small OpenID Connect provider. Passkeys need HTTPS, so use a domain. Set it up at /setup right after installing, as the first visitor becomes its admin.

templates.name: prometheus
templates.title: Prometheus
templates.description: Collects metrics from this host and from every service with nepfleet.metrics labels. It has no login, so it isn't published: use the grafana template to look at it.

templates.name: uptime-kuma
templates.title: Uptime Kuma + AutoKuma
templates.description: Uptime monitoring and status pages. AutoKuma creates monitors from kuma.* labels. Install it once for the whole fleet, or once per stack for a stack-local status page.

inputs.name: KUMA_USERNAME
inputs.title: Admin user
inputs.description: Created on Kuma's first start, so its setup screen is never open; sign in with it, and AutoKuma does too.

templates.name: volume-backup
templates.title: Volume backups (docker-volume-backup)
templates.description: Scheduled, age-encrypted backups of the Docker volumes on this host, to a local folder and optionally over SSH/SFTP (e.g. a Storage Box). Containers labelled docker-volume-backup.stop-during-backup=true are stopped during the backup for consistency. Host folders (media, photos) are not included; back them up with backrest.

inputs.name: SSH_HOST_NAME
inputs.title: SSH/SFTP host for off-host copies (empty = local only)

inputs.name: SSH_HOST_PUBLIC_KEY
inputs.title: SSH host public key
inputs.description: Required with SSH. One line from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 -p <port> <host>`, without the host name, e.g. "ssh-ed25519 AAAA…".

inputs.name: EXCLUDE_REGEXP
inputs.title: Paths to skip (regular expression)
inputs.description: In addition to the volumes templates mark backup false, which NepFleet leaves out by itself. Matched against /backup/volumes/<name>/...

inputs.name: NOTIFICATION_URLS
inputs.title: Notification URLs (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: failed backups are reported to NepFleet, which sends them to the fleet's notification channels. Set comma separated shoutrrr URLs (e.g. discord://token@webhookid) only to send somewhere else instead.

templates.name: watchtower
templates.title: Watchtower (maintained fork)
templates.description: Image update notifications for containers NepFleet does not manage. Monitor-only by default, because in-place updates bypass the fleet repository and cannot be rolled back.

inputs.name: WATCHTOWER_MODE
inputs.title: Mode
inputs.description: "true" = monitor only (notify). "false" = update labelled containers in place.

inputs.name: NOTIFICATION_URL
inputs.title: Notification URL (override)
inputs.description: Leave empty: notifications go to NepFleet, which sends them to the fleet's notification channels. Set a shoutrrr URL (e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/my-topic) only to send somewhere else instead.

templates.name: actual
templates.title: Actual Budget
templates.description: Local-first personal finance and envelope budgeting. Sign in with the server password from the stack's inputs.

inputs.name: SERVER_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Server password
inputs.description: The password you sign in to Actual with, set before the domain opens so nobody else can claim the server. Taken on the first start only; a server that already has a password keeps it. Change it later in Actual's settings.

templates.name: adguard-home
templates.title: AdGuard Home
templates.description: DNS ad and tracker blocking for the whole local network, and local DNS records. It starts set up, with the admin from the stack's inputs, so no setup wizard is offered. Point your router's DNS at this host. For trusted names at home, add a DNS rewrite under Filters: *.home.example.org (Caddy's wildcard domain) to the server's LAN address.

inputs.name: BIND_ADDR
inputs.title: Address DNS listens on (0.0.0.0 = all; this host's LAN IP if systemd-resolved holds port 53)

inputs.name: DNS_PORT
inputs.title: DNS port (53 for devices to use it)

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Admin user name
inputs.description: Used only on the first start. Later, change it in AdGuard Home's settings file.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: You sign in to the web UI with it. Used only on the first start; stacks set up through the old wizard keep the admin they have.

templates.name: audiobookshelf
templates.title: Audiobookshelf
templates.description: Audiobook and podcast server with apps for phones, progress sync and podcast downloads. The root user comes from the stack's inputs.

inputs.name: AUDIOBOOKS_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder with your audiobooks
inputs.description: Mounted writable, so uploads, metadata embedding and deleting files from the app work.

inputs.name: PODCASTS_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder for podcasts (downloads go here)

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Root user name
inputs.description: Audiobookshelf's root (admin) user, created on the first start only. Changing it later does not rename the user; do that in the app.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Root user password
inputs.description: Password of the root user, set on the first start only. Changing it later does not change the password; do that in the app.

templates.name: bookstack
templates.title: BookStack
templates.description: Wiki and documentation, organised in shelves, books and pages. Sign in with the admin e-mail and password you choose here.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin e-mail
inputs.description: You sign in to BookStack with it. Taken on the first start only, where it replaces the default admin@admin.com; change it later in BookStack.

inputs.name: ADMIN_NAME
inputs.title: Admin name
inputs.description: The admin's display name. Taken on the first start only.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet; at least 8 characters. Taken on the first start only, where it replaces the default password; change it later in BookStack.

templates.name: forgejo
templates.title: Forgejo + Actions runner
templates.description: Self-hosted git forge with a registered Forgejo Actions runner. Jobs run in an isolated Docker-in-Docker daemon, never on the host's Docker.

inputs.name: SSH_PORT
inputs.title: Host port for git over SSH

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Admin user name (you sign in with it)
inputs.description: Not admin, which Forgejo reserves. Created on first start, or on the next apply of an existing stack; renaming it later here creates another admin.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password (at least 8 characters)
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet. The admin is created with it when that account doesn't exist yet; change the password later in Forgejo.

inputs.name: RUNNER_LABELS
inputs.title: Actions runner labels, separated by commas (label:docker://image)

inputs.name: RUNNER_CAPACITY
inputs.title: Actions jobs that run at once

inputs.name: OIDC_ISSUER
inputs.title: Identity provider (OpenID Connect issuer), for signing in
inputs.description: Pocket ID, Authelia and others. Register a client with the redirect URL https://<domain>/user/oauth2/<name>/callback. It must be reachable when the stack is applied: Forgejo checks it then. People link it to their account; new accounts still need an admin, as registration stays off. Leave empty for none.

inputs.name: OIDC_NAME
inputs.title: Its name on the sign-in page

templates.name: garage
templates.title: Garage
templates.description: Lightweight S3-compatible object storage, as a single node. It creates a bucket and an access key (GK + ACCESS_KEY_ID, with SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: the values you set) on first start. Apps and backups that speak S3 can store their files there. More keys and buckets: docker exec into the container and use the garage command.

inputs.name: ACCESS_KEY_ID
inputs.title: Access key ID (without GK)
inputs.description: 32 hex characters, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 16. Apps use GK followed by it as their access key ID.

inputs.name: SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
inputs.title: Secret access key
inputs.description: 64 hex characters, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 32. Apps use it as their secret key. Kept encrypted in the fleet.

templates.name: hermes-agent
templates.title: Hermes Agent
templates.description: Nous Research's AI agent, reached through messaging apps. It acts on what people send it, so set who may talk to it. Its browser dashboard isn't included, as it stores API keys and has no login of its own.

inputs.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
inputs.title: OpenRouter API key
inputs.description: For other providers, see its docs and set them in the data volume's configuration.

inputs.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS
inputs.title: Telegram user IDs who may use it, separated by commas

inputs.name: DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS
inputs.title: Discord user IDs who may use it, separated by commas

templates.name: homeassistant
templates.title: Home Assistant
templates.description: Home automation. Runs on host networking for device discovery (mDNS, SSDP), and Caddy reaches it through host.docker.internal. Not for swarm.

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Owner user name (you sign in with it)
inputs.description: Lowercase, no spaces. The owner is created on the first start, so the onboarding wizard is never open; a stack that is onboarded already keeps its users as they are. Change the password later in Home Assistant.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Owner password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet. Taken only on the first start, to create the owner.

inputs.name: ZIGBEE_DEVICE
inputs.title: Zigbee USB stick for ZHA (e.g. SkyConnect, Sonoff)
inputs.description: Pick its /dev/serial/by-id path; Home Assistant sees the same path, so ZHA keeps working across reboots. After replugging the stick, restart the stack.

templates.name: homebox
templates.title: Homebox
templates.description: Home inventory and organisation.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin e-mail
inputs.description: You sign in to Homebox with it. Homebox registers this account on its first start only; later changes here don't reach it (change it in Homebox).

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: At least 6 characters. Taken on the first start only, when Homebox registers the admin; change it in Homebox afterwards.

inputs.name: ALLOW_REGISTRATION
inputs.title: Allow registration
inputs.description: Lets anyone who reaches Homebox create an account. The admin is created without it; invite others from Homebox instead.

inputs.name: LABEL_PRINT_COMMAND
inputs.title: Command that prints a label on the server
inputs.description: Runs in the container for Print on Server; empty turns that off (browser printing always works). Homebox passes the label image's file name, see its label maker documentation. Label images can go to /labels, the volume <stack>-labels, which other stacks can mount.

templates.name: imgproxy
templates.title: imgproxy
templates.description: Resizes and converts images on the fly, for apps that support it. Only signed URLs work (with the KEY and SALT you set, which the apps get too), and only images from ALLOWED_SOURCES, so it is no open proxy. Apps on this host reach it at imgproxy:8080 on the ingress network; the domain serves it to browsers.

inputs.name: ALLOWED_SOURCES
inputs.title: Where images may come from, as URL prefixes separated by commas
inputs.description: For example http://garage:3900/images/ for a Garage bucket on this host, or https://media.example.org/. Anything else is refused.

inputs.name: KEY
inputs.title: URL signing key
inputs.description: Hex, at least 32 characters, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 32. Apps that sign image URLs need the same key. Kept encrypted in the fleet.

inputs.name: SALT
inputs.title: URL signing salt
inputs.description: Hex, at least 32 characters, e.g. from: openssl rand -hex 32 (another one). Apps that sign image URLs need the same salt.

templates.name: immich
templates.title: Immich (+ Power Tools)
templates.description: Photo and video backup with machine learning. Immich Power Tools (bulk management, login with your Immich account) is an optional profile. Photos live in UPLOAD_PATH on the host; back that folder up with backrest (volume-backup covers the database).

inputs.name: UPLOAD_PATH
inputs.title: Host folder for photos and videos

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin email
inputs.description: Immich's admin, created on its first start so the "create admin account" page is never open to whoever finds the domain first. You sign in with this email. Only used while Immich has no admin; later changes go in Immich.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: The admin's password, set on Immich's first start only; change it in Immich later.

inputs.name: ADMIN_NAME
inputs.title: Admin name
inputs.description: The admin's display name, set on Immich's first start only.

templates.name: jellyfin
templates.title: Jellyfin
templates.description: Media server. Mount your media read-only. Pick a GPU for hardware transcoding.

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Admin user
inputs.description: Created before Jellyfin is first reachable, so its startup wizard is never open on the domain. Taken only on the first start; later changes go in Jellyfin's own settings.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: You sign in with it. Taken only on the first start (stacks whose wizard is already done keep their users); change it later in Jellyfin.

inputs.name: GPU
inputs.title: Hardware transcoding (VAAPI/QSV on Intel or AMD, NVENC on NVIDIA)

templates.name: kutt
templates.title: Kutt
templates.description: URL shortener (SQLite).

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin email
inputs.description: Kutt's admin, created on its first start so its "create admin" page is never open to whoever finds the domain first. Sign in with it. Taken only on the first start; change it in Kutt's settings later.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: 8 to 64 characters (Kutt's sign-in allows no other length). Taken only on the first start; change it in Kutt's settings later.

inputs.name: DISALLOW_REGISTRATION
inputs.title: Disable public registration
inputs.description: Kutt's sign-up also needs mail, which this template does not set up.

templates.name: mastodon
templates.title: Mastodon
templates.description: Fediverse server. The domain becomes part of every account's name and can never change after the first start. Sign-ups need mail, so set SMTP. For push notifications, make keys with: docker compose exec web bundle exec rails mastodon:webpush:generate_vapid_key.

inputs.name: DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain (can never change after the first start)

templates.name: matrix
templates.title: Matrix
templates.description: Chat with Synapse and the Element web client. Registration is off: create the first user with register_new_matrix_user in the synapse container, using REGISTRATION_SECRET from the stack's secrets. The domain becomes part of every user's name and can't change later.

inputs.name: ELEMENT_DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain of the Element web client, e.g. chat.example.org

templates.name: mealie
templates.title: Mealie
templates.description: Recipe manager and meal planner that imports recipes from any URL. Sign in as admin with the e-mail and password you set here.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin e-mail
inputs.description: You sign in to Mealie with it. Mealie's default admin (changeme@example.com / MyPassword) gets it once, while that login still works (on the first start); an admin changed earlier stays as it is. Change it later in Mealie.

inputs.name: ADMIN_NAME
inputs.title: Admin full name
inputs.description: Set once, like the e-mail.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: At least 8 characters. Set once, like the e-mail, so the default password never stays; change it later in Mealie.

templates.name: metube
templates.title: MeTube (yt-dlp web UI)
templates.description: Download videos and audio with yt-dlp from the browser. No built-in login, so keep it on the home network or behind forward auth.

templates.name: n8n
templates.title: n8n
templates.description: Workflow automation with a visual editor, webhooks and hundreds of integrations.

inputs.name: DOMAIN
inputs.title: Domain (also the base URL of webhooks)

inputs.name: OWNER_EMAIL
inputs.title: Owner e-mail
inputs.description: You sign in to n8n with it, as its owner.

inputs.name: OWNER_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Owner password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet; n8n gets only its bcrypt hash, and takes it on every start, so a new one here replaces the old.

templates.name: navidrome
templates.title: Navidrome
templates.description: Music streaming server with a Subsonic-compatible API. Music is mounted read-only.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password (user admin)
inputs.description: You sign in as admin with it. Kept encrypted in the fleet. Navidrome creates admin on its first start; change the password later in Navidrome.

templates.name: ntfy
templates.title: ntfy
templates.description: Push notifications to phones and desktops over HTTP, for NepFleet and anything else (ntfy://<domain>/<topic> in shoutrrr). Access is closed by default: sign in as admin with the password you set (ADMIN_PASSWORD) and create users or tokens for publishers.

inputs.name: UPSTREAM_BASE_URL
inputs.title: Upstream for iOS push (e.g. https://ntfy.sh; empty = none, iPhones then poll)
inputs.description: With an upstream, ntfy.sh learns message IDs (not contents) to wake iPhones.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD

templates.name: open-webui
templates.title: Open WebUI (+ Ollama, LiteLLM)
templates.description: Chat UI for language models. Profiles add Ollama (local models) and/or LiteLLM, an OpenAI-compatible gateway to cloud providers and other runtimes (vLLM, llama.cpp, LocalAI); models are configured in litellm.yaml. Its admin is the one set here; others sign up only if you allow it.

inputs.name: ENABLE_SIGNUP
inputs.title: Allow sign-ups
inputs.description: Applies on first start only; Open WebUI stores it, so later changes go through its Admin settings.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin e-mail (you sign in with it)

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password

templates.name: openbao
templates.title: OpenBao
templates.description: A secrets manager with Vault's API, for apps that read their secrets from Vault (NepFleet itself doesn't need it: its secrets are SOPS files). It initialises itself on the first start and creates an admin from the stack's inputs (userpass auth, a policy with full access); the root token it used is revoked and never shown. It unseals itself on every start with a key NepFleet generated (static seal), so restarts and image updates need nobody. That key sits encrypted in the fleet repository and in the stack's environment on the host: whoever has root on the host or the fleet's SOPS key can read the vault, as with every other stack's data.

inputs.name: ADMIN_USER
inputs.title: Admin user
inputs.description: You sign in with it (method Username in the UI, or bao login -method=userpass). Taken on the first start only; stacks set up before version 1.0 keep their own logins.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: Kept encrypted in the fleet; at least 12 characters. Taken on the first start only; change it later in OpenBao (auth/userpass/users/<user>/password). Stacks set up before version 1.0 don't use it.

migrations.description: OpenBao now unseals itself with a generated key (static seal). A stack initialised by hand has to move its seal once: after this upgrade it is sealed, run docker exec -it <stack>-openbao-1 bao operator unseal -migrate as often as your threshold, with your unseal keys. From then on it unseals itself; your old unseal keys become recovery keys and your logins stay as they are.

templates.name: openclaw
templates.title: OpenClaw
templates.description: AI assistant gateway for messaging apps. It runs tools for whoever can message it, so think hard before connecting personal accounts, and consider egress mode enforce. Set it up with: docker compose exec openclaw node dist/index.js onboard. Not published on the network.

templates.name: pihole

templates.description: DNS ad and tracker blocking for the whole local network. Point your router's DNS (or each device's) at this host. If systemd-resolved already uses port 53, set BIND_ADDR to this host's LAN address. Sign in to the web UI with the password you set (WEB_PASSWORD).

inputs.description: For example home.example.org, the same as Caddy's wildcard domain: that name and every name under it go to HOME_ADDRESS, and never upstream. The reserved home.arpa changes nothing.

inputs.name: HOME_ADDRESS

inputs.description: For example 192.168.1.20. Empty answers the home domain with "no such name".

inputs.name: WEB_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Web UI password

templates.name: rabbitmq
templates.title: RabbitMQ
templates.description: A message broker for apps and your own services. Its management UI is behind your domain (sign in as admin with the password you set, ADMIN_PASSWORD). Services on the ingress network reach AMQP at rabbitmq:5672; it is also published on this host's loopback, or on the LAN when you set AMQP_BIND to 0.0.0.0. Not for Swarm yet: swarm publishes ports on every address, so the loopback default can't hold there.

inputs.name: AMQP_BIND
inputs.title: Address AMQP is published on (127.0.0.1 = this host only; 0.0.0.0 = the LAN too)
inputs.description: Services on the ingress network reach it at rabbitmq:5672 either way. On the LAN, clients need the admin or their own credentials.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: You sign in to the management UI as admin with it. Kept encrypted in the fleet. RabbitMQ takes it on its first start; change it later in RabbitMQ.

Sign in at https://DOMAIN/login?url=https://DOMAIN/rc/ (the dashboard tile links there); scripts use rclone rc --url https://DOMAIN/rc/.

templates.name: sure
templates.title: Sure
templates.description: Personal finance: accounts, budgets, investments and net worth (the community fork of Maybe Finance). The first account, a super admin, comes from the admin inputs and sign-up is closed by default. Back up this stack's secrets with the fleet's: the ENCRYPTION_* keys encrypt bank provider tokens, which are unreadable without them. It sends no usage data to Sure's PostHog project. Market data lookups tell Yahoo Finance or Twelve Data which currencies and tickers you hold, and AI features, when set up, send transactions to that provider.

inputs.name: ADMIN_EMAIL
inputs.title: Admin email
inputs.description: The first account, a super admin, is created with it on the first start, so sign-up never needs to be open. Sign in with it; Sure then asks for your name, country and currency. Only used while Sure has no account yet: later changes do not change the account.

inputs.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
inputs.title: Admin password
inputs.description: At least 8 characters. Only used when the first account is created; change it later in Sure's settings.

inputs.name: ONBOARDING

inputs.description: closed: nobody can sign up, only the admin above signs in. invite_only: people with an invite code or invitation from an existing user. open: anyone who reaches the domain.

inputs.name: OIDC_ISSUER
inputs.title: Identity provider (OpenID Connect issuer), for signing in
inputs.description: Pocket ID, Authelia and others. Register a client with the redirect URL https://<domain>/auth/openid_connect/callback. The provider must report the email as verified. Leave empty for none.

inputs.name: OIDC_BUTTON_LABEL
inputs.title: The provider's button on the sign-in page

inputs.name: OIDC_NEW_ACCOUNTS

inputs.description: link_only: only people who already have an account (same email) can sign in through the provider. create_and_link: the provider can create accounts too.

inputs.name: OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS
